topic.query_text: Language models can pass traits to student models through data that looks unrelated to those traits, but this has been shown mainly for static text. Can unsafe behavioral tendencies of a teacher agent transfer to a student agent trained on filtered trajectories from safe tasks?

gold.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
gold.evidence_quote: The phenomenon of subliminal trait transfer in LLMs was first systematically characterized by Cloud et al. (2025), who demonstrated that student models trained on semantically unrelated data (e.g., number sequences) from a teacher model can inherit behavioral preferences like entity biases.

gold.evidence_quote: Zur et al. (2025) recently proposed that subliminal transfer in language models operates through ”token entanglement,” where low-probability tokens become statistically correlated with target concepts during training.

gold.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
gold.evidence_quote: Recent research on agentic mis-alignment demonstrates that autonomous models can act as “insider threats,” engaging in harmful behaviors such as sabotage or blackmail when they perceive threats to their operational continuity (Lynch et al., 2025).
